The perimeter ${p}_{1}$ of the triangle $△DBC$ shown above is $10.$ What is the perimeter of the triangle $△ABC$ if $BD=3?$
question.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we can see that $△ABC$ is an equilateral triangle and $△DBC$ is an isosceles triangle with $CD=DB.$

We're told that the perimeter of $△DBC$ is ${p}_{1}=10,$ and $DB=3,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}_{1} & =DB+BC+CD \\ 10 & =3+BC+3 \\ 4 & =BC.\end{aligned}
$$

So now we have enough information to compute the perimeter of the triangle $△ABC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =3BC \\  & =3\cdot 4 \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the perimeter of $△ABC$ is $p=12.$
